headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty plunged as Indian markets recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold Indian stocks en-masse
Global risks and rising oil prices sparked significant capital outflows
Concerns over global rate hikes impacted investor sentiment
The market is closed today in observance of Gandhi Jayanti
whatHappening: The Sensex dropped 570.59 points while the Nifty closed at 22,421.95 in the last session
Indian benchmark shares logged their worst month since March due to global economic pressures
Reliance Industries announced a major ₹1 trillion investment plan for Andhra Pradesh
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance underwent a leadership transition with a new MD & CEO appointment
summary: Indian markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti following a volatile session where benchmarks extended their losing streak to eight consecutive weeks. Significant foreign investor selling and global macro concerns led to the Sensex and Nifty posting their longest weekly decline in 25 years. Despite the downturn, corporate activity remained high with major investment announcements from Reliance and leadership changes at ICICI Prudential Life and HDFC Bank.
